events.text: A world too poor to pay in faith asks your Weavers of Fate for woven fortunes, promising a temple in a thousand years.

effects.log: You give it. A thousand years later, there is a temple, small and full.
You refuse. The world goes quiet.
You give half. Half a temple, half full.

events.text: A god of Fortune offers you a thread spun from a god's last hope, the kind of thing that makes a house famous across the sky, for nearly all your faith.

effects.log: You take it. Gods cross domains to see it.
You refuse. Another house takes it.

ok.log: You get it for half. Fortune is impressed.

events.text: The looms of the Hall of Fate falls when its pantheon loses a war, and its keeper comes to your Weavers of Fate with nothing but their old rites.

effects.log: You take them in. Their worlds follow them to you.
You take the worlds. The keeper fades.
You turn them away. Gods hear of it.

events.text: A clerk of the Heavenly Court comes to your Weavers of Fate to count your faith against the Book of Fates, and frowns at the difference.

effects.log: The clerk finds nothing and says so to the Court.

choices.text: Offer the clerk a little faith

effects.log: The clerk accepts. The Book will remember.

ok.log: You win every page.

events.text: Your head weaver has fallen in love with a mortal below and wants to leave your Weavers of Fate to live a mortal life with them.

choices.text: Let them go, with a blessing

effects.log: You bless them. They live a short, bright life below.

choices.text: Ask them to wait an age

effects.log: They wait. The mortal does not. It is your fault, a little.
You forbid it. They go anyway.

events.text: In the worlds below, people are building temples to your Weavers of Fate that you never blessed, and selling false woven fortunes in your name.

effects.log: You bless them. They become true.

choices.text: Send a dream to end it

effects.log: You send a dream. The false priests flee.
You let them. Some of the faith still reaches you.

events.text: The oldest pilgrim of your Weavers of Fate, a soul who came every age for ten thousand years, has stopped coming. Their world has ended.

choices.text: Keep their place at the altar

effects.log: You keep their place. The other pilgrims bow to it.

choices.text: Go and find where they went

effects.log: You find them on the Pale Ferry, and say goodbye.

choices.text: Give their place to a new world

effects.log: You give it to a new world. Life goes on, even for gods.

events.text: Faith comes to your Weavers of Fate that is faintly dark: stolen on the Unlit Sun and passed on to you, worth more than it should be.

effects.log: You take it. The Unlit Sun notices your house.

choices.text: Send it back where it was stolen

effects.log: You trace it home and return it.
The Court thanks you, and watches you.

events.text: A god born only an age ago wants to learn to keep a house of faith at your Weavers of Fate, and knows nothing at all.

effects.log: You teach them. In an age they keep a house of their own.
They work for nothing and learn hard.

choices.text: Send them to a pantheon's house

effects.log: You send them with a word. They remember.

events.text: The sun of the sky goes dark for a day, and every soul on the roads between domains crowds into your Weavers of Fate for light.

effects.log: You open them all. The souls never forget your lamps.
They pay, frightened.
You bar them. Your house is safe. The souls are not.

events.text: A pantheon proposes taking your Weavers of Fate into its own temples: its blessing, your name, its priests counting your faith.

effects.log: You agree. The house is greater and not quite yours.
You refuse, politely, forever.

choices.text: Agree, but keep the counting yourself

ok.log: You keep the counting. It is yours in all but name.

events.text: The Feast of Domains comes to your road, and every house is expected to send an offering to the table. Yours is the smallest house there.

effects.log: Your offering is spoken of for an age.
It is plain and the gods like it.
Your pilgrims make it together. The gods are moved.

events.text: The Star Market comes for a debt of faith your Weavers of Fate owes from the god who kept it before you, ages ago.

effects.log: You pay. The market trusts you after.

ok.log: You find the old tally.

effects.log: You refuse. The market remembers.

events.text: A god of an Elder Lineage offers to take your Weavers of Fate for more faith than it has ever earned. They say they like the light there.

effects.log: You refuse. They ask again in an age.

ok.log: They want what sleeps under the altar.

effects.log: They consider it. You realise they might pay. You do not sell.

events.text: A quiet age at your Weavers of Fate: no wars, no plagues, no famous gods. Only the pilgrims and woven fortunes and the slow gold sky.

effects.log: You rest. Gods forget how.
You plan, and the next age goes well.

choices.text: Close the doors for a while

effects.log: You close for a little while.

events.text: A herald of a far pantheon arrives at your Weavers of Fate: their worlds want woven fortunes before the next age turns, more than you have ever given.

choices.text: Promise it and work for it

effects.log: You promise, and keep it, barely.
You give half, truly.
You decline. The herald is cold.

events.text: A small god sneaks into your Weavers of Fate and takes a thread spun from a god's last hope, or what you let everyone think it was.

choices.text: Let them keep the false one

effects.log: You say nothing. A small god is very proud of a fake.
You follow them to a ruined temple and leave the real one there.
Their pantheon punishes them. You feel worse than you expected.

events.text: A mortal saint, carried up on the prayers of a whole world, walks into your Weavers of Fate and kneels to you, mistaking you for a far greater god.

effects.log: You tell them. They laugh and kneel anyway.
You let them. Their world prays to you now.

choices.text: Take them to the god they meant

effects.log: You take them. That god owes you now.

events.text: Two gods of rival domains quarrel in your Weavers of Fate, and the floor of the house cracks with the weight of it.

choices.text: Send the bill to their pantheons

effects.log: Both pantheons pay, blaming each other.

ok.log: They stop. Gods are not used to being stood between.

effects.log: You show them the door. They settle it somewhere else.

events.text: Your head weaver has found a truer way to make woven fortunes, and asks whether it will be the house's rite or their own.

effects.log: You honour it as theirs. They serve the house forever.
You make it the house's. They serve, less warmly.

choices.text: Give it to every house on the road

effects.log: You give it away. Every house of faith is better.

events.text: Your Weavers of Fate has stood for an age among the gods. Your pilgrims have planned an offering, and it is enormous and slightly on fire.

effects.log: You accept it. The fire is put out, mostly.

choices.text: Rest the house for a day

effects.log: You rest the house. The pilgrims sing outside.

choices.text: Carve every pilgrim's world into the threshold

effects.log: The threshold is the house's treasure now.

events.text: Your Cloud-Tea House has a second floor now, and ministers' clerks have begun to hold their quarrels upstairs, where they think nobody listens.

effects.log: You listen. Tea is not the only thing you sell now.
You never listen. The clerks trust your house above all others.

events.text: A minister asks to hold the Court's spring council in your Cloud-Tea House, in the room with the view of the falls of cloud.

effects.log: You host it. Your house is in the Court's records now.
You decline. Neutral houses are rare above the clouds.

events.text: The pledges in your Lantern Pawn's vault have started to whisper at night. A few of them, you suspect, were never meant to be redeemed.

ok.log: You find the cursed ones and seal them.

fail.log: One of them follows you home.

effects.log: You ignore them. Mostly they ignore you.

events.text: An immortal comes to redeem a pledge left with your Lantern Pawn eight thousand years ago, by someone who is not them.

effects.log: You give it. Somebody's story is finished.
They have none, and leave, and you are never sure.

events.text: Your Peach Inn has a room nobody will sleep in, where a Sovereign once stayed. Guests pay to stand in the doorway.

effects.log: They pay. It is the best room in the house and nobody sleeps in it.
A tired drifter sleeps there and dreams of thrones.

events.text: The Peach Inn is the only inn on the drifting road where factions at war will both stay. The Jade Court asks you to keep it so.

effects.log: You promise. It is a heavy promise.
You take one. Half the road stops at your door.

events.text: A physician of the Lotus Halls comes into your pharmacy and buys one of everything, to see what you are doing that they are not.

effects.log: You tell them. The Halls send patients to you after.
You keep them. They never find out.

events.text: The tribulation season is coming, and immortals are stockpiling your meridian pills. You could sell all of them in a day.

effects.log: You ration them so everyone gets some.
You sell them all by noon.

events.text: A duellist brings a blade back to your Star Forge: it broke in a duel, and they lost. They want the price back, and an apology.

effects.log: You give both. They come back with the next blade.

ok.log: It was struck wrong, not forged wrong. They leave quietly.

events.text: A falling star comes down within sight of your Star Forge, and three forges race for it.

ok.log: It is yours. The forge has a new heart.

choices.text: Let it fall where it falls

effects.log: It falls into the sea of cloud and nobody has it.

events.text: Your Convoy House has more skiffs than captains, and a reaver who served under the King of the Cloud Road asks to captain one.

effects.log: You hire them. Your skiffs are not boarded again.
You refuse. They go back to the mist.

events.text: The Jade Court wants your Convoy House to carry its tribute to the Divine Realm's threshold, a run no convoy has ever finished.

ok.log: You finish it. The Court remembers.

fail.log: You come back with half the convoy.

effects.log: You decline. Someone else tries.

events.text: An heir of the Eight Houses sends back a cloud-silk robe from your looms because it is too plain, and their rival heir wears one just like it the next day, proudly.

choices.text: Make the next one plainer still

effects.log: You do. It becomes the fashion.
You make it gaudy. They love it.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries want new robes for every minister, from your looms, by the next audit.

effects.log: You weave it all. Your looms are the Court's now.
You weave half honestly.

events.text: Your Hall of Offerings has a second altar now, and a world you have never heard of has started leaving its whole harvest on it.

effects.log: They believe you saved them. You did not. You do now.
You accept it. The hall is rich.

events.text: Two pantheons at war both want to leave their offerings at your hall, because it is the one place neither will burn.

effects.log: You take both. Your hall is a sanctuary now.
You take one side.

events.text: A vow held at your House of Vows has been broken below, and the one who broke it asks you to hide it from the gods it was sworn to.

effects.log: You hide it. You are a keeper of secrets now.
The broken vow is heard. Justice follows.

events.text: The oldest vow in your keeping, never kept or broken, has begun to glow. Somewhere, someone is about to keep it.

effects.log: It is kept. The light fills the house for an age.
You find them: a child below. You bless them.

events.text: A soul who walked from a dead world asks to stay at your Pilgrims' Rest forever, because there is nowhere left to go.

effects.log: They stay, and become the rest's gentlest keeper.

choices.text: Send them on the Pale Ferry

effects.log: You send them on, gently.

events.text: The road between domains moves, and now your Pilgrims' Rest stands at a crossroads of four pantheons.

effects.log: All four come. Your rest is the busiest in the sky.
They pay, and resent it.

events.text: A god of plague comes to your Temple of Mending in disguise, to see who is undoing their work.

effects.log: You treat them. They leave one world alone, after.

ok.log: You unmask them, and they flee.

events.text: The Life Domain itself sends a messenger: your temple has answered more prayers for the sick than its own halls this age, and it would like to know how.

effects.log: You show them. The Domain is a little kinder after.
You keep it. The Domain watches you.

events.text: A blade consecrated at your Forge-Temple turned on the hero who held it. Their family below is praying for vengeance against your forge.

choices.text: Answer their prayer with a new blade

effects.log: You send a new blade, and a blessing.

ok.log: The hero was not a hero. The blade knew.

events.text: A hero who has died nine times comes to your Forge-Temple for a tenth blade, and asks you to make it the last.

effects.log: You forge it. They do not die again. They grow old.
You refuse. They go to another forge.

events.text: The Pale Ferry of the Death Domain says your Ferry of Pilgrims is carrying souls that are not quite dead.

effects.log: You stop. The Domain is satisfied.
You keep carrying them. Some of them wake up.

events.text: One of your ferries went into the dark between worlds and did not come out. Its lantern came back alone.

ok.log: You bring it back, and everyone on it.

choices.text: Light a lantern for it every night

effects.log: You light one every night. After an age, it comes back on its own.

events.text: A thread on your loom has snapped, and a small world's luck is unravelling. You can feel it from here.

ok.log: You reweave it. The world never knew.

choices.text: Let the Hall of Fate handle it

effects.log: The Hall handles it, slowly.

events.text: The Hall of Fate asks that your Weavers of Fate stop weaving fortunes for worlds that can pay, and weave for the ones that cannot.

effects.log: You agree. Your looms are poorer and the sky brighter.
You refuse. The Hall watches your looms.

events.text: The first year of your house above the clouds. Somewhere below, the shop you left has a new keeper and the same old sign. Up here nobody knows your name, and the isle's other houses send a cup of something sour to welcome you.

effects.log: You send back your best. By spring the other houses nod to you.
You send nothing. They notice that too.

events.text: The first age of your house among the gods. The worlds below that knew your old shop pray now to a god who keeps houses, and do not know it is you.

effects.log: You answer the old prayers first. They feel it.
You begin with new worlds. The old ones find you anyway.

events.text: Under the lip of a drifting isle, where the cloud thins to nothing, something glows like a lamp behind paper: a cloud vein, stones grown out of the isle's own underside, running back into the dark.

effects.log: You hang your seal on the isle's underside and hire skiff-crews to dig. The first chest of stones comes up within the season.

choices.text: Sell the place to a faction

effects.log: A faction steward pays you well for a map and your silence.
You tell the isle's elders. The vein is theirs, and they will not forget whose it could have been.

events.text: Between two domains, where neither god has looked in an age, a seam of godstone runs through the sky like a vein through a wrist.

effects.log: You set your sign on it. Small gods come to cut it for you, for a share of faith.

choices.text: Sell the secret to a pantheon

effects.log: A pantheon pays in faith for your silence.

choices.text: Give it to the small gods of the border

effects.log: You give it to them. They will build you a shrine of it.

events.text: A rockfall in the hills of this world has opened a seam that glows faintly, a vein of stones grown in the land you live in.

choices.text: Stake the claim and open a mine

effects.log: You stake it and hire diggers. The first cart rolls out within the season.

choices.text: Sell the secret to a lord

effects.log: A lord pays well for the map.
The village digs it together, and names the hill for you.
